notes: reading: lowercase Revised Romanization of the standard pronunciation, word by word (no sound changes across spaces); tensification is not written; ㅢ is always ui; nouns keep h after ㄱ/ㄷ/ㅂ (식후 sikhu, 역할 yeokhal) while verbs, adjectives and adverbs aspirate (축하하다 chukahada, 급히 geupi). Use the same rules for dialogue and passage readings.

id: ko. + romanization of each word joined by hyphens; a dictionary-form 하다 word is split before -hada (운동하다 -> ko.undong-hada). Suffixes mark the only real clashes: ko.jeotda-stir, ko.munui-pattern, ko.machida-finish, ko.butda-stick, ko.bullyang-amount, ko.gachi-value.

register: 해요체 in C-D (반말 only appears as a topic in D8-r02 and is taught in E3); 합니다체 is introduced in E1-01 and the plain written style (-ㄴ/는다) in E8-06; from then on articles, notices, diaries and essays in E-F readers may use the written style.

homographs kept apart: 눈 (eye) is a word while snow is the phrase 눈이 오다; 절 in C12-04 is 'temple'; 차례 (turn, D4) vs 차례를 지내다 (ancestral rite, C12). Standalone 팔, 공, 반, 사이, 달, 시 were avoided because they collide with A-B number, time and location words.

grammar: a pattern taught again with a new function is labelled 'second use' or by its function (e.g. -아/어서 sequence D1-05 vs reason D2-01); lessons whose topic says 'Review lesson' recycle earlier patterns on purpose.
